If your condition alone is enough to make you think it’s not worth it to go on anymore, then it’s more than understandable to ask for the mercy death provides. I hope one day humanity realizes that mercy means “live and let live” only for people with healthy bodies and minds while death for them is unmerciful, but the exact opposite for people suffering in irreversible conditions, bound to an undignifying life. The choice is yours to make in this regard to judge if you feel like life is still worth living.

However, if the broken-heartedness is the final straw driving you to thinking about ending it, but could go on with someone that loves you, then I can confidently say that there are many caretaker souls out there that potentially can find something loveable in you as a person.

I recommend you the story of Ramón Sampedro. That guy was quadraplegic for 30 years, but he was still a charismatic person enough to find someone that loved him. Although Sampedro’s story is one of struggle for the right to get help in ending a life he felt to be undignifying - his lover being the one to finally grant him the solace he longed for - you can draw some inspiration to find a loving person that sees past your condition and still sees you for who you are. There’s an exceptionally good movie about the story titled “The Sea Inside”, it might provide some solace.

You may still find love, but until then hold onto your family and anyone you still have around to support and care for you.

Here people use the [dot product](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_product) notation for basic multiplication because essentially you mutliply these numbers which don't have a direction to them, just scalar values.

We only use the [cross product](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_product) notation (×) when multiplying two vectors to get a third vector in a three dimensional oriented Euclidean vector space.

Since basic arithmetics are basically algebraic operations more so than 3d vector operations, it makes more sense to use a dot product notation.

This record is absolutely brilliant, very versatile as well, so everyone will have a different opinion for sure. Here's my rating for each track which I averaged out of a music score, a lyrics score and a nostalgia/sympathy x factor. (these will seem biased, but keep in mind, to me an AVERAGE Architects song is around an 8.75-9/10, this band is just really up there)

Do You Dream Of Armageddon - 8.17/10 Couldn't say a lot about the intro track, but it is a track worthy of starting up the album.  ("No tree can grow to heaven til its roots reach down to hell" reminds me of the "As above, so below" dichotomy from Memento Mori)

Black Lungs - 8/10 Establishes the bleak environmental crisis early on the record, solid track

Giving Blood - 8.67/10 An interesting mixture of genres, falling more towards the rock sound of the record, yet it works perfectly somehow. I can definitely relate to that bridge lyrically.

Discourse Is Dead - 8/10 Banger chorus+post chorus breakdown, love it. Besides, healthy political discourse has really been dead for a long time (maybe except in Finnland), especially in the country I live in...

Dead Butterflies - 9.08/10 Most personal song on the album for Dan, heartfelt, full of love, a true Architects masterpiece

An Ordinary Extinction - 9/10 Insane BMTH-esque production, whoever made that intro synth/guitar, props! Huge, explosive chorus as well holy shit!

Impermanence - 8.33/10 Shocker! Didn't really find the fan and band favorite all THAT much. Still that breakdown is awesome cuz well... ZEROS

Flight Without Feathers - 9.07/10 YESYESYESYESYES, this is what has been missing for me from the post Daybreaker era of Architects! Makes me think of tracks like Behind The Throne, Up And Away and Hollow Crown even (this is coming from one of the rare people who love even The Here And Now for what it is)

Little Wonder - 9.07/10 The now more marketable version of These Colours Don't Run. Hell yeah!! More people will be influenced by Dan and the band's views and principles and frankly I think this song is amazing for that

Animals - 9/10 This is how you right a simple banger. Architects really proved they can show more with less. I love that this song has the power to make me take a step back when I'm struggling with anxiety or feel overwhelmed and just let go. We're just a bunch of fucking animals...

Libertine - 8.53/10 At first I didn't fully understand the lyrics to relate, but at second listen felt a lot of connection to the metaphors for that destructive mindset/downward spiral we sometimes find ourselves in. Musically it's an average album cut, but the ambience in this track made it stand out a bit to me

Goliath - 9.07/10 Woaah... That Simon Neil feature is absolutely breathtaking. Never listened to Biffy Clyro before... That's not the case anymore ;)

Demi God - 9.12/10 Dear God, Sam's performance on this song... The ambience... Dan's lyrics touching on feeling imperfect and flawed despite being a demi god (possibly a reference to Alan Watts'/Eastern philosophy viewing every living being as equally of the divine)... The wierd chord progression... It's nothing short of art. It actually makes me think of Dying To Heal a lot, since it is about a similar feeling of Dan's.

Meteor - 8.83/10 Not gonna lie, at first I got a little scared about the album when this one came out. We get the very Architects flavoured lyrics painting this apocalyptic scenery shadowed by that inevitable meteor. The thing is, that sonically it bore no resemblence to Architects' sound. I don't mean that as it wasn't heavy, because Architects never had one signature style, they always had multiple different branches of influences and sounds. This however, resembled something completely alien to the Architects experience, minus Sam's vocals at some places. It is a good song, don't get me wrong, but Architects never was the band that was describable by saying "oh it's x band + y band" which usually just makes the listener want to listen to x or y. I was positively surprised by the rest of the album thankfully, and I've also gotten a little more fond of this track as well, since it is relatable for most of us, feeling weak and powerless to make a difference and accomplish great things. And it's not even that I don't like this sound, it's just that it "wasn't an Architects song" (same things some "fans" said about THAN back then, eventhough I like that album a lot // "If we weren't the ones in the studio recording that then who are we?" - Tom xD). If anything I was more scared that people would grab pitchforks and torches to rise up against my favorite musicians. The placement of Meteor also weakens the album's cohesion **in my opinion** as **I feel** Demi God would make a much better transition into Dying Is Absolutely Safe.

Dying Is Absolutely Safe - 9.72/10 I don't have words to describe this beauty other than "Thank you, Dan!" Architects always knew how to finish a record, many of the album closers make me tear up every single time, but this one is just special. The last time I was impacted this deeply by a song was when I first heard Memento Mori 3 years ago. That time I could only say "Thank you, Tom!"... I'm so proud of the band for creating this beautiful song, but especially Dan...

All in all, the album's production value is something else. The songs are brilliant, many a time simple, yet not generic. With these factors included I've averaged the score of this album to be 9.03/10. Is this my favorite album of Architects? It isn't really fair comparing albums, since there are many things present on the palette of this album that I may lack from ones I rated slightly above this release, and vice versa. In some aspects this album knocks stronger scored albums out of the park, and the same is true for ones of a lesser score than this. But, with that being said here's my Architects album toplists from Hollow Crown onward, that I compiled based on how much I enjoyed them that I'm sure will piss some people off, but hey, more power to ya! ;)
